one_sided.formula: k = t'(gamma, df=n-1, nc=z_P*sqrt(n)) / sqrt(n), where t' is the noncentral t distribution and z_P = Phi^-1(P)
one_sided.method: Exact — computed via scipy.stats.nct.ppf (noncentral t inverse CDF). Validated against independent Monte Carlo simulation (2,000,000 trials): n=10, P=0.95, gamma=0.95 -> formula k=2.911, simulated actual coverage=0.9502 (target 0.95).

two_sided.formula: k = z_((1+P)/2) * sqrt( (n-1)*(1+1/n) / chi2(1-gamma, n-1) )  [Howe (1969) approximation]
two_sided.method: Howe's approximation — the standard method used across quality-engineering texts (incl. Montgomery) for two-sided normal tolerance limits, since the exact two-sided factor has no closed form and requires iterative numerical integration. Validated against independent Monte Carlo simulation (3,000,000 trials) across n=2, 10, 25: simulated actual confidence landed within 0.3 percentage points of the gamma target in every case, including the worst case at n=2.

note: P = minimum proportion of population covered; gamma = confidence level. Layout matches CRE Handbook Appendix H.1/H.2 and CSSBB Handbook Appendix J.1/J.2 conventions (P and gamma as the two selectable parameters, n as the row index).
